## Week 1 Friday's In-class Assignment {.scrollable}

ADD SOLUTIONS

1.  Find a JSON data file online and load it into R using either the local download or the URL. (5 minutes)

2.  Print the column names of the data frame. (2 minutes)

3.  Print the first 10 rows of the data frame such that all columns are visible. (2 minutes)

4.  Print the mode, i.e. `mode()`, of each column of the data frame. (1 minute)

5.  Print the typeof, i.e. `typeof()`, or class, i.e. `class()`, of each column of the data frame. (1 minute)

6.  Pick one column that is character-valued and truncate the character strings to retain only the first 2 characters. (3 minutes)

7.  Create a new numeric column representing the number of characters (character length) of one character-valued column. (3 minutes)

## Extract: structured data

- **readr** package which is within **tidyverse** package

- `read_csv()` function if delimiter is comma

- `read_delim()` function if alternative delimiter

  - `delim =` to specific delimiter in quotes

- `read_fwf()` function is fixed-width

**Real Data: [Data Science Jobs Postings provided by Glassdoor via web-scraping by Kaggle user Rashik Rahman](https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/5nqg2dk8uym5u87s9rv1gq10mtxnybij.txt)**

## Extract: semi-structured data as JSON

- **jsonlite** package

- `fromJSON()` function

  - `flatten =` argument or `flatten()` function may help remove nesting(s)

**Real Data: [Greatest of All Time Artists and their Songs provided by Billboard and Spotify](https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/omj8z0gb2zivcuhn5fhqt0n8ahvxwes4.json)**

## Extract: semi-structured data as XLSX

- **openxlsx** package

- `read.xslx()` function

  - `sheet =` argument to specify which sheet to read

**Real Data: [Highest Grossing Films provided by Box Office Mojo, an IMDB company](https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/drhbcntw0g73u29m79t9yl8q4oocgir7.xlsx)**

## Extract: semi-structured data as HTML {.scrollable}

- **rvest** package for **web-scraping**

- [SelectorGadget](https://selectorgadget.com/) tool for finding CSS tags

- If page has specific CSS tags, `read_html() |>` `html_elements() |>` `html_text2()`

  - if CSS tags are not working, `html_elements(xpath =)` argument may help\
  - XPath may require lots of trial-and-error

- If page has data in tables, `read_html() |>` `html_table()`

**Real Data: <https://champaignil.devnetwedge.com/parcel/view/922116304005/2025>**

## Extract: semi-structured data as JSON {.scrollable}

- **httr** package for making http requests and **API calls**

- Application Programming Interface (API) is a set of rules that allows one software application to interact with another

- Primarily designed for developers to build applications that can access features or data

- Many APIs are available for free, but many require an API key or token

`GET() |>`\
`content(as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8") |>`\
`fromJSON(flatten = TRUE)`

- 200\* Status Code means the request was successful

- 400\* Status Code means the client or user made an error

- 500\* Status Code means the server encountered an error

**Real Data (no API key needed): [National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration / National Weather Service (NOAA/NWS) API](https://api.weather.gov)**

- [National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration / National Weather Service (NOAA/NWS) API Guide](https://weather-gov.github.io/api/general-faqs)

**Real Data (API key needed): [OpenWeatherMap API](https://openweathermap.org/api)**

## Data Dictionary {.scrollable}

- A document that describes the structure, content, and meaning of data elements in a dataset

- Provides information about each variable, including its name, type, format, and any relevant metadata

- Written in Markdown syntax and saved as .Rmd

- Includes original source of the data, URLs, provider information, and Markdown table

| Field Name        | Data Type | Description                       | Example    |
|-------------------|-----------|-----------------------------------|------------|
| id_number         | numeric   | unique identifier for the student | 238371753  |
| first_name        | character | first name of the student         | montana    |
| last_name         | character | last name of the student          | williams   |
| birth_date        | date      | date of birth of the student      | 01/01/2004 |
| employment_status | character | current employment status         | part-time  |

## Extract: unstructured data as text

- `readLines()` base R function

- May require `stopwords()` function within **stopwords** package

**Real Data: [The Complete Works of William Shakespeare provided by Project Gutenberg](https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/19qhj5fmlvo1a3mwf22gx31j5h9oh9o8.txt)**

**Real Data: [Trump Tweets 2017-2019 provided by Trump Twitter Archive and Twitter](https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/sf65zjc2s9xhpy6npnw21edai61evhnl.txt)**

## Extract: unstructured data as audio

- **tuneR** package
  - `readWave()` function for .wav files
- **av** package
  - `read_audio_bin`()\` function for .mp3 files
  - `av_audio_extract()` function for extracting audio from video files

**Real Data: [Audio file provided by Loopmasters](https://uofi.box.com/shared/static/vmmaky1fe5wgv9z4vnzrsln1why3jg8u.wav)**

## In-class Assignment {.scrollable}

1.  Extract JSON data from The Open Movie Database API based on your own query <http://www.omdbapi.com> (you will have to register for a free API key)

2.  Create a data dictionary for the extracted data and save it as a .Rmd file named `data-dictionary-open-movie-database-api.Rmd`

3.  Now, create a data dictionary for each data in the data-and-sources.Rmd file and save each as a .Rmd file named `data-dictionary-{data-name}.Rmd` where `{data-name}` is the name of the data file before the provider information and without the extension and without curly braces. For example, for the "Shipping Arrivals at Cape of Good Hope provided by IMF Portwatch and Oxford University" data, the file should be named `data-dictionary-shipping-arrivals-at-cape-of-good-hope.Rmd`.
